html:
The Mbyá are a Guarani people of the Atlantic forest, living today in eastern Paraguay, Misiones in Argentina, and southern Brazil as far as the coast of São Paulo and Rio Grande do Sul. The map shows their wide range across this region.

They are farmers of maize, manioc and beans in forest clearings, and their religion is rich in sung prayers and stories about a land without evil, a promised place that drew Guarani groups on long journeys. Many Guarani were gathered into the Jesuit reductions in the 1600s and 1700s; the Mbyá ancestors were largely those who stayed out of the missions in the forest. As forests were cleared in the 1900s, Mbyá families were pushed onto small plots and roadside camps. Their relatives include the Guarani and the Kaiowá.
